THE GAME

Horror · Investigation · Lo-fi

Trash Nights is a lo-fi first-person horror game. Autumn, 1998: you take the night shift on garbage truck No. 7 in Maple Hollow, a quiet suburb whose last crew quit without notice.

Clock in at the depot, take truck No. 7 and listen to Dot on the radio. Drive, stop, throw the bags in the hopper, run the compactor. Clear the street and get back before 4 AM. The routine works without a single scare, and that is what makes the scares hit.

Every bag says something about whoever threw it out. Clues go in the glove box and in the notebook the last crew left behind: house by house notes, the rules of the route, and lines that get more nervous until they stop mid sentence.

WHAT'S INSIDE

01

One street a night

Each night is a new street in Maple Hollow, 11 PM to 4 AM, and each night is stranger than the last.

02

Truck No. 7

A garbage truck you actually drive, with a hopper, a compactor and a reverse beeper that everyone on the street can hear.

03

The trash tells the story

Real clues and false leads sit in the bags. Every neighbor's trash looks guilty for an innocent reason. Except one.

04

Nothing supernatural

No monsters. Just people, noises and things out of place. If the crickets stop, get back in the truck.

05

Six nights, seven endings

Gather evidence, accuse someone over the radio and live with what the county police find. Or just finish your shift.

06

PS1 look, VHS filter

Low-poly streets, chunky pixels and an optional VHS filter, straight out of a tape you should not have rented.
